delta.comment: Contract replanning (operator-directed, 2026-08-19): late-identifier reconciliation workflow defined. Closes the dangling obligation where 134.004-T's LATE-SURFACING THREAD criterion delegated reconciliation to "Stage's C6 intake responsibility" with no task defining it, making every threadless `N/A` permanent under the single-write invariant. Added: retrieval from Ship-owned residual-risk records via the deferred entry ID join key, Stage-authority in-place reconciliation (no Ship write, C5 carve-out unweakened), anti-duplication, non-blocking, and idempotence rules. Added dependency on 134.004-T (content ordering, not checksum serialization); 134.007-T deliberately excluded with rationale. Size M -> L for genuine scope growth.

Readiness fix cycle 3 (review of 904c46b9, P1): added dependency on 134.007-T. The prior exclusion rationale was "the fix-ci carrier is threadless by nature -- a review thread never surfaces inside a fix-ci run -- so it originates no late identifier", which reasoned from the false threadless-only premise. fix-ci Step 6.5 re-queries for threads opened during the fix phase, so a CI finding captured with review-thread ID N/A can gain a thread inside the same run; fix-ci therefore originates late identifiers and its run/closure records are a retrieval source this task must name. RETRIEVAL SOURCE criterion updated accordingly. Content ordering edge only - 134.007-T is template-only with no dogfood or manifest entry, so hardening H4 serialization does not apply.

PR #372 Copilot review-fix cycle 1 — thread PRRT_kwDORzpWpM6amwJt (comment 3816508932), line 42. Duplicate remediation said the reconciliation "removes" the duplicate entries; it now ARCHIVES them into the earliest surviving entry, on two independent grounds. (1) Tool protocol: backlogit's CLI exposes `stash archive` and no `stash remove` subcommand at all, and the MCP `backlogit_stash_remove` is explicitly deprecated in favour of `backlogit_stash_archive` — the instruction as written was not executable. (2) Evidence: a duplicate deferred entry is proof that a discovery lookup returned a false absence, so destroying it destroys the diagnostic along with any source ref the duplicate carries and the survivor does not. Line 45 now requires the deliberation to record all three audit outcomes — reconciled identifiers, explicit no-result reconciliation, and the archived duplicate IDs with their merge disposition — so archival is auditable rather than silent. B14's mapped obligations and the AUTHORITY-OWNER MAP were aligned to the archive verb, with an explicit warning in the map not to read this verb off hardening H2 (which describes Ship's separate, already-shipped post-merge cleanup).

PR #372 review-fix cycle 3 (P1-2). Stage intake split into TWO independently triggered obligations: (A) UNCONDITIONAL duplicate detection over every triaged deferred entry regardless of field population, and (B) N/A-triggered late-identifier reconciliation. Previously a single N/A trigger covered both, so a duplicate captured with every identifier populated -- the common PR-review-comment case -- was never examined, while 134.004-T's fail-safe asserted this task scanned "unconditionally". Discovery-status tokens are an ACCELERATOR (seed candidate IDs), never the trigger, since duplicates from a false-absence lookup carry no token. ANTI-DUPLICATION is now governed by (A). Audit output extended THREE -> FOUR outcomes, adding CLEAN DUPLICATE SCAN: under an unconditional trigger an unrecorded clean scan is indistinguishable from one never run.
